tagline: A short routine for everyday skin.

audience.primary: Adults who want a short daily skincare routine
needs: A few products that fit a morning and evening step
Clear limits on what a product does not do

positioning: Aurora Skincare keeps the routine short: a few products with named ingredients and specific use notes, for adults who want skincare copy they can check.

avoid: medical claims (cure, heal, diagnose, clinically proven, FDA-approved, medical-grade)
hype or guarantees (miracle, guaranteed, overnight results, 100% effective, world's best)
ingredient claims that the product page does not support

visual.image_style: soft daylight, clean product photography, no clinical imagery

selling_points: A three-step morning and evening routine
Ingredient names written in plain language
Use notes that say what each product is for
Quiet packaging and a limited color palette
trust_signals: Full ingredient list on every product

home.intent: Introduce Aurora Skincare and route shoppers to the routine collection.

sections.intent: Show the brand name, tagline, and primary color.
List the four selling points as short, specific claims.
Show trust signals. Do not add phrases listed in tone.avoid.

collection.intent: Help shoppers scan Aurora products by routine step.

sections.intent: Restate the positioning in one sentence.
Show title, price, and one selling point per product.

product.intent: Explain one product with specific, non-medical copy.

sections.intent: Use positioning and selling points. Honor tone.avoid.
Ingredient names, use notes, and trust signals.
